title: Handle Selection even while annotation is open + reset to last state …
summary: Since the last plan (commit `55130a8`), the PR stops a note from moving the Discover pane when you've already left the note editor: for example, if you close Discover in the middle of editing a note and later delete that note, Discover now stays as it is. Overall, on a computer, finishing a note (Save or Cancel) puts the Discover pane back the way it was before the note editor opened. Before, it always opened the Discover list afterwards, even if Discover had been closed and you started the note from the verse toolbar. Phones already worked this way and should not change.

links.label: Issue 1876: Verse toolbar should hide while a new note is being written

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer, with the browser window maximized (most tests are about the wide, computer layout). Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you have the newest version
setup.body: The app caches itself, so it can show an older version. Do a hard refresh once: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email. You'll be sent a code, so use an email inbox you can check. A private/incognito window gives you a clean start if anything looks odd.

sections.title: Notes started with Discover closed
sections.intro: Discover is the side panel with notes, playlists and other content for the chapter. In these tests it starts closed.

setup.title: Close Discover
setup.body: If the Discover panel is open beside the chapter, close it, so you see only the chapter text (with the small "Discover John" section below it).

tests.title: Saving a note started from the verse toolbar returns to the plain chapter
tests.why: This is the main change. Before, Discover would open to its list after saving.
steps: Click verse **16** in John 3 so it's selected and the verse toolbar appears.
In the verse toolbar, choose **Note**.
Type `Test note one` in the note editor.
Click **Save**.
expected: An "Annotation saved" message appears.
The note editor closes and the Discover panel is closed again. You're back to just the chapter, like before you pressed Note.
Verse 16 is no longer selected.

tests.title: Cancelling a note started from the verse toolbar returns to the plain chapter
steps: Click verse **17** so it's selected.
In the verse toolbar, choose **Note**.
Type `Will cancel` in the note editor.
Click **Cancel**.
expected: The note editor closes and the Discover panel stays closed. Discover's list does not open.
No note is saved for verse 17.
Verse 17 is still selected, and the verse toolbar is showing again so you can pick another action.

tests.title: Editing a note from the verse toolbar returns to the plain chapter
tests.before: Uses the note on verse 16 from the first test in this section.
steps: Click verse **16** so the verse toolbar appears. Your note `Test note one` is listed in it.
Next to the note, click the **Annotation options** menu (the three dots) and choose **Edit**.
Change the text to `Test note one edited` and click **Save**.
expected: The note editor closes and the Discover panel is closed again. It does not open to its list.
Selecting verse 16 again shows the note with the new text.
tests.why: On the plan for commit `55130a8` this passed, but the tester noted: "Should not close discover panel i guess." The PR returns Discover to how it was before the note (closed, in this test). If you think Discover should stay open here instead, say so in your notes.

tests.title: Using Create under the chapter returns to the plain chapter
tests.why: Another way to start a note while Discover is closed. On the plan for commit `55130a8` this passed, but the tester noted: "Should not close discover panel i guess." The PR returns Discover to how it was before the note (closed, in this test). If you think Discover should stay open here instead, say so in your notes.
steps: Click verse **18** so it's selected.
Scroll down below the chapter text to the "Discover John" section and click **+ Create**.
Type `Test note two` in the note editor and click **Save**.
expected: The note editor closes and the Discover panel is closed again.
The note shows up for verse 18.

setup.title: Open Discover
setup.body: Open the Discover panel: select any verse and choose **Discover** in the verse toolbar, or click **Show All** in the "Discover John" section below the chapter. Leave it open on its main list.

tests.title: Saving a note started inside Discover returns to the Discover list
steps: Select verse **19** in the chapter.
In the Discover panel, click **+ Create** and choose **Annotation**.
Type `Test note three` and click **Save**.
expected: The note editor closes and the Discover panel shows its main list again (it stays open).
`Test note three` appears in the list.

tests.title: Editing a note from the Discover list returns to the Discover list
steps: In the Discover list, find `Test note three`.
Click its **Annotation options** menu (three dots) and choose **Edit**.
Change the text to `Test note three edited` and click **Save**.
Repeat: choose **Edit** on the same note again, then click **Cancel**.
expected: After Save, Discover shows its list again with the updated text.
After Cancel, Discover also shows its list again, and the note text is unchanged.

tests.title: Using Note from the verse toolbar while Discover is open returns to the Discover list
steps: With Discover still open, click verse **20** in the chapter.
In the verse toolbar, choose **Note**.
Type `Test note four` and click **Save**.
expected: The note editor closes and Discover shows its main list again. It does not close.

tests.title: A playing playlist comes back after a note
tests.why: Changed since commit `55130a8`: the PR now has automated checks that the playing playlist comes back after both Save and Cancel, and the author asks testers to flag it if returning to the player looks wrong in practice. So this test now checks Cancel too.
tests.before: You need at least one playlist. If you have none, create one in Discover with **+ Create** → **Playlist**, add a passage and save it.
steps: In Discover, start playing a playlist so the playlist player shows in the panel.
In the chapter, select a verse and choose **Note** in the verse toolbar.
Type `During playlist` and click **Save**.
Select another verse, choose **Note** again, type anything, and click **Cancel**.
expected: After Save, the note editor closes and Discover shows the playing playlist again, not the main Discover list.
After Cancel, Discover also shows the playing playlist again.

sections.title: Leaving the note editor early
sections.intro: New since commit `55130a8`. These tests close Discover or leave the editor in the middle of editing a note, then finish with that note some other way.

tests.title: Deleting a note after closing Discover mid-edit keeps Discover where it is
tests.why: New since commit `55130a8`. Before, deleting a note you'd started editing could jump Discover back to how it was before the edit (here: closing it), even though you had already left the editor.
tests.before: Start with Discover closed. Uses a note you can delete, such as `Test note two` on verse 18 from an earlier test.
steps: Click verse **18** so the verse toolbar appears, open the note's **Annotation options** menu (three dots) and choose **Edit**. The note editor opens in the Discover panel.
Without saving or cancelling, close the Discover panel.
Open Discover again on its main list (for example, click **Show All** in the "Discover John" section below the chapter).
In the Discover list, find `Test note two`, open its **Annotation options** menu and choose **Delete**, then confirm.
expected: The note is deleted and disappears from the list.
Discover stays open on its main list. It does not close by itself.

tests.title: Editing again after closing Discover mid-edit works normally
tests.why: New since commit `55130a8`. Checks that a note abandoned by closing Discover doesn't get stuck or saved by accident.
tests.before: Start with Discover open on its main list. Uses `Test note three edited` from the earlier section.
steps: In the Discover list, open the **Annotation options** menu on `Test note three edited` and choose **Edit**.
Change the text to `Should not be saved`, but don't click Save. Close the Discover panel instead.
Open Discover again (click **Show All** below the chapter).
Choose **Edit** on the same note again, change the text to `Test note three final` and click **Save**.
expected: After reopening Discover in step 3, the note still reads `Test note three edited`. The unsaved text was not saved.
After the final Save, the editor closes, Discover shows its main list, and the note reads `Test note three final`.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: On a phone, saving and cancelling a note still return to where you were
tests.why: Phones already returned to the previous screen before this PR. The PR changes the same code, so check it still does.
tests.before: Use a phone, or make your browser window very narrow (under about 480 pixels wide) and reload.
steps: Open **John 3** in the reader with Discover closed.
Tap verse **21**, then tap **Note** in the verse toolbar.
Type `Phone note` and tap **Save**.
Tap verse **22**, tap **Note**, type anything, and tap **Cancel**.
expected: After Save, you're back on the chapter, and the note is saved for verse 21.
After Cancel, you're back on the chapter, verse 22 is still selected, and nothing was saved.

tests.title: The verse toolbar hides while a new note is being written
tests.why: From issue 1876, which this PR's branch is named for. It should still work.
steps: On a computer, select verse **23** and choose **Note**.
While the editor is open, also click verse **24** in the chapter.
Type `Two verses` and click **Save**.
expected: While the note editor is open, the verse toolbar is hidden, but the verses stay highlighted as selected.
The editor's verse reference above the text updates to include verse 24 when you select it.
The saved note is attached to verses 23–24.

tests.title: A failed save keeps the note open
steps: Select a verse and choose **Note**. Type `Offline note`.
Turn off Wi-Fi (or turn on airplane mode).
Click **Save**.
Turn Wi-Fi back on afterwards.
expected: Either the note saves (it may be kept on the device until you're back online), or the message "Couldn't save the annotation." appears and the editor stays open with your text still in it.
Your text is never lost without a message.
